about: D4-B acceptance roster (#5340 S3). implemented = lib tests registered, not passed; verdicts come from scripts/check_herdr_s3_d4b_manifest.py --require now|full --results. Pieces: 1 G-HOME, 2 G-POST, 3 H7 sources, 4 H6 restart/H9 durable, 5 wall-clock, 6 release reset and after.

cases.what: worker holder restart on the same root rehydrates its O store and posts each owed piece once
a rebooted standby holder restores its channel's persisted input before its drain reads turns as known, and does not leave while turn, queue, owed or POST remain
cases.evidence_scope: one process through the production start_channel_homes(Standby) over real PG and a real runtime root: two reclaiming rows held by this node, one with a queue left on disk, one with a corrupt placeholder file; checks the drain blocker turn_unreadable, turn_running, owed_unreadable and the failed restore staying turn_unreadable with both rows Reclaiming. No writer actor runs, so owed stays unreadable and the Reclaimed CAS is not reached; that and an inflight-row restore are left to the s3fence acceptance step in s3_real

cases.what: releasing gateway holder restarts and leaves only through an allowed reset
cases.evidence_scope: two GW process generations: the first dies inside the reset call; checks the injected LegacyReset's refuse/apply/retry order through real PG, boot watch and drain; Applied is the callback's Ok(()) and shows no managed-session reset, provider-session delete, process cleanup or their idempotence

cases.what: released target adopts through the runtime driver, not a test-side DB adopt
cases.evidence_scope: the target's boot watch over real PG with the runtime's BootPort::reading port, and the REST worker's start_channel_homes; the release is seeded in PG, the adopt is the watch's; unrestored, two renewal periods leave the row released

cases.what: a delegation's reclaim returns through the gateway's own watch: the home-bound writer is joined before the row goes, then a writer under the gateway's authority is ready and posts again; a gateway booting under another node's row or unreadable rows starts no first writer for it
cases.evidence_scope: two child processes over real PG: a gateway booted with no row whose candidate watch drains the delegate, releases and ends its writer; a worker that adopts through its watch, posts and drains the parent's reclaim; the same gateway watch removing the reclaimed row and starting a writer that is ready and posts. The gateway child assembles its writers as the runtime does (ChannelWriters over start_managed, an acquired gateway gate), not through run_bot. A gateway child restarted on its store's root while a worker child holds the row runs the runtime's first spawn (ChannelWriters::start_boot) after its watch's first round and, until the next round, hosts no writer, takes no work and posts nothing while the worker keeps posting. In process: a reclaimed boot's start order, a writer that ends after its start, an unreadable row, unreadable boot rows admitting no first writer. A CAS-stale race is not covered

cases.what: both nodes restart; only the PG holder opens and POST intervals never overlap
holder dies, CLI force, both nodes reboot; the orphaned row holds every consumer
a target alive through the holder's death and the force never gains readiness or admission
a new GW boots with the gateway role while the existing MINI keeps its old config; PG holder and epoch stay unchanged
a real gateway/standby switch stops and resumes the writer
a lone Prepared blocks the leave; the replayed source settles it Posted with no new POST
a lone Prepared with readable history and no candidate settles NotFound
a lone Prepared whose history read fails settles Unresolved
a lone Codex unsealed unit blocks the leave until it seals and posts
a lone pending bind or waiting boundary blocks the leave; the bind posts once it resolves
releasing tail posts, the reset succeeds and the row leaves as released
cases.evidence_scope: one GW process generation's drain, not dynamic delegate registration or a standby lifecycle; checks the injected LegacyReset's refuse/apply/retry order through real PG, boot watch and drain; Applied is the callback's Ok(()) and shows no managed-session reset, provider-session delete, process cleanup or their idempotence

cases.what: a counted POST alone keeps the row draining while the projection is zero
an unreadable POST count keeps the row draining until it reads zero
optional: delivery is still admitted during the first responsibility check
accepts re-reads the home gate after the writer is ready
force keeps the old holder's durable spool and Prepared; the target takes none of it
real H, POST timeout and F: admission ends at H, the POST is joined, force only after F
